explainer.heading: The story in brief
explainer.body: The narrator spends the autumn hunting season with friends at a chateau. His friends love practical jokes, so when they give him a princely reception and laugh too much at dinner, he is sure a joke is planned against him. He spends the night guarding against it — and his own precautions cause the “joke” the next morning.
explainer.example: Theme: irony — trying too hard to avoid something brings it about.
explainer.hook: He made his own uncomfortable bed!

explainer.heading: Suspicion
explainer.body: They fire rifles, embrace him and make much of him. He tells himself, “Look out, old ferret!” (meaning himself). All evening he watches every word and gesture, even suspecting the helpers. The whole household escorts him to his room and calls a chorus of “Good night”; he hears laughter and whispers in the corridor.
explainer.example: “I scented a practical joke in the air, just as a dog scents game.”

explainer.heading: The night of precautions
explainer.body: He lights all the candles on the mantelpiece, inspects every article, shuts the large wooden shutters, draws the velvet curtains and puts a chair in front. He fears a cold shower from above or the bed collapsing, so he drags the mattress and bedclothes into the middle of the room facing the door, puts out the candles and finally falls asleep.

explainer.heading: The morning
explainer.body: He wakes with a heavy body falling on him and a burning liquid on his face, with a crash like a sideboard of dishes falling. He hits the face he feels, gets blows in return and runs into the corridor — it is broad daylight. The valet, bringing his morning tea, had tripped over the bed in the middle of the floor and spilt the breakfast on him. Everyone laughed that day.
explainer.example: The valet also got the surprise of his life.

explainer.heading: Vocabulary
explainer.body: Adjectives of personality: suspicious, cautious, watchful, restless, mischievous. Suffixes -ation / -ion / -th: suspect → suspicion, prepare → preparation, strong → strength, warm → warmth. Collocations (adjective + noun): practical joke, broad daylight, princely reception. Idioms with senses: smell a rat (suspect something), see eye to eye, keep an eye on.

explainer.heading: Grammar: reported speech
explainer.body: In reported speech the tense usually moves one step back and pronouns/time words change: am → was, will → would, can → could, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, here → there.
explainer.example: Direct: He said, “I am on my guard.” → Reported: He said that he was on his guard.
explainer.hook: Tense back, pronoun shift, time words change.

explainer.heading: Writing & author
explainer.body: A notice: name of institution, the word NOTICE, date, heading, short body (what, when, where, who to contact), name and designation of the writer, often boxed. Guy de Maupassant was a French writer, one of the greatest short-story writers; works include “Boule de Suif”, “The Necklace”, “The Horla” and “Bel-Ami”.

questions.q: Where did the narrator spend the hunting season?
questions.why: A chateau with friends who loved practical jokes.

questions.q: What made the narrator suspicious on arrival?
questions.why: They fired rifles and embraced him.
He warns himself to be alert.

questions.q: What did the narrator first do inside the room?
options: Stood still holding a candle and looked around
questions.ans: Stood still holding a candle and looked around
questions.why: He remained standing, without moving a step.

questions.q: Why did he light all the candles on the mantelpiece?
options: In case his candle suddenly went out
questions.ans: In case his candle suddenly went out
questions.why: He feared being left in darkness.

questions.q: Why did he shut the shutters and put a chair before the curtains?
options: So nothing could come at him from outside
questions.ans: So nothing could come at him from outside
questions.why: He wanted nothing to fear from outside.

questions.q: Where did he finally make his bed?
options: In the middle of the room facing the door
questions.ans: In the middle of the room facing the door

questions.q: What woke him in the morning?
options: A heavy body falling on him and burning liquid on his face
questions.ans: A heavy body falling on him and burning liquid on his face
questions.why: The valet fell over his bed.

questions.q: Was there really a practical joke planned?
options: No — the accident happened because of his own precautions
Yes, the friends hid in the room
questions.ans: No — the accident happened because of his own precautions
questions.why: The valet tripped over his improvised bed.

questions.q: What is the irony in the story?
options: His efforts to avoid being laughed at made everyone laugh at him
questions.ans: His efforts to avoid being laughed at made everyone laugh at him
questions.why: His precautions caused the funny incident.

questions.q: At what time did the incident happen?
Report: He said, “I will sleep here.”
options: He said that he will sleep here.
He said that he would sleep there.
He said that I would sleep there.
questions.ans: He said that he would sleep there.

questions.q: Why did the princely reception make the narrator suspicious?
questions.model: His friends were fond of practical jokes. The over-warm welcome and excessive laughing made him feel they had a joke planned in which he would be the victim.
points: Too much welcome/laughter → thought he’d be the victim

questions.q: How did the valet land on top of the narrator?
questions.model: While bringing the narrator’s morning tea, the valet tripped over the bed the narrator had made in the middle of the room, fell on him and spilt the tea on his face.
points: Tripped over the bed in the middle of the room

questions.q: Describe the precautions the narrator took during the night and explain the irony of the story.
questions.model: He lit all the candles, inspected every article, closed the shutters, drew the velvet curtains and placed a chair before them. Fearing a trick with the bed, he dragged the mattress and bedclothes to the middle of the room facing the door and slept there. Ironically, there was no joke at all. In the morning the valet tripped over this improvised bed and spilt hot tea on him, and the narrator fought him thinking it was a prank. His efforts to avoid being laughed at made everyone laugh at him.
points: Bed moved to the middle of the room
Irony: no joke, but his precautions caused the laughable accident
